To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) The SUSY QCD one-loop corrections to the production of Higgs boson in the MSSM can be quite large in the parameter space that has survived all current experimental constraints; (ii) In the parameter space that is allowed by current collider searches and dark matter detection, the SUSY-QCD one-loop corrections can be as large as −9%.

The complete one-loop SUSY QCD contributions to the $pp\to \mathrm{b}\overline{\mathrm{b}} \mathrm{h}$ process at the LHC can reach up to −9%, depending on the values of tan β, mA, and the sparticle masses.
